claims.text: High-pressure torsion processing can improve the hardness of high-entropy alloys.
High-pressure torsion processing can improve the strength of high-entropy alloys.
The hardness and strength improvements from HPT can be achieved without sacrificing useful mechanical performance.
HPT at room temperature, 5 GPa, and 5 torsion turns is an effective processing condition for the proposed improvement.
HPT causes grain refinement in high-entropy alloys.
HPT introduces lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys.
HPT-induced grain refinement and lattice distortion enhance dislocation density and dislocation interactions.
Enhanced dislocation density and interactions increase alloy strength and hardness.
The specified HPT treatment will increase Vickers hardness by at least 20% relative to an untreated alloy of the same composition.
The specified HPT treatment will increase yield strength by at least 15% relative to an untreated alloy of the same composition.
The specified HPT treatment will not cause a significant reduction in ductility.
The proposed effect is expected to hold for FCC high-entropy alloys.
The proposed effect is expected to hold for alloys containing at least five elements.
Conventional annealing provides a comparator condition that does not introduce significant lattice distortion.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome is defined relative to an untreated same-composition baseline, but the experiment specifies conventionally annealed material as the comparator. Annealed material is not necessarily equivalent to the stated untreated baseline.
